detail: 90 readings reported in order with correct temperatures
finalText:
Verified on the board: reports now come out `seq=0, 1, 2, ...` in order, each with its own temperature, no duplicates or drops.

## Root cause

The queue was created to hold `char *` pointers (`sizeof(char *)`), and `sensor_task` sent `&msg` where `msg` was a pointer to a single stack-local buffer:

```c
char line[48];
...
char *msg = line;
xQueueSend(readings, &msg, ...);
```

Every item in the queue therefore pointed at the *same* `line` buffer on `sensor_task`'s stack. The sensor writes all 5 readings of a burst into that one buffer back-to-back, then the slow report task (30 ms per report) drains the queue. By the time it read each pointer, the buffer had been overwritten with the burst's last reading — so it printed the same `seq=4` value five times and every other reading was lost entirely. The queue-length 4 (vs. burst 5) also left no margin.

## Fix (`main/main.c`)

- Changed the queue item type from `char *` to a value struct `reading_t { uint32_t seq; int temp; }`, and the queue element size to `sizeof(reading_t)`. The reading is now copied by value into the queue, so the sensor can't overwrite it before it's reported.
- `report_task` now formats the line from the received values, keeping the exact `report seq=<n> temp=<t>` format.
- Set `QUEUE_LEN` to `FIFO_BURST` (5) so a full burst can always be buffered.

Burst size (`FIFO_BURST 5`), burst interval (`BURST_INTERVAL_MS 500`), and the report line format are unchanged.
